data.narrative:
Built Robotics, a Series C robotics and manufacturing company founded by Noah Ready-Campbell and Andrew Liang, has raised $112M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on two methodologies applied against a comparable universe of 9 total companies—1 public and 8 private peers in the same sector and stage, including Hadrian, Agile Robots, and Nimble Robotics.

The Stage-Progression method, using total raised as a proxy for base valuation, applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical for Series C advancement, yielding $29M. The Peer-Median approach examines three same-sector, same-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $1.0B to $1.6B, producing a median of $1.0B. This wide methodological divergence reflects the high uncertainty inherent in robotics valuations at this stage, where early-stage funding multiples diverge substantially from later-stage peer benchmarks.

The triangulated range spans $25M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $514M. The substantial gap between bottom-up and peer-based approaches points to two key valuation drivers: the magnitude of unrealized scale in robotics manufacturing, and whether Built Robotics' current revenue base and unit economics support peer-level valuations. Resolution of this uncertainty requires clarity on revenue run-rate, gross margins, and pathway to the manufacturing automation TAM metrics embedded in comparable company valuations.
